text: OpenClaw defines itself as a personal AI assistant running on the user's own devices, while the Gateway is the control plane rather than the product itself.
OpenClaw uses a single long-lived Gateway to own messaging surfaces, while control clients and nodes connect to it over WebSocket.
An OpenClaw agent run covers intake, context assembly, model inference, tool execution, streaming replies, and persistence, with runs serialized per session.
The OpenClaw workspace is the agent's default working directory and context home, but it is not a hard sandbox.
The Gateway owns session state, routes inbound messages into sessions based on source, and stores runtime session rows in a per-agent SQLite database.
One Gateway can run multiple logically isolated agents, each with its own workspace, state directory, and session history, while bindings route accounts and peers to agents.
Tools are callable actions, Skills provide instructions, and Plugins add runtime capabilities including tools, providers, channels, hooks, and packaged skills.
OpenClaw nodes are paired peripherals rather than gateways, and approved system.run calls can be forwarded from the Gateway to a node host.
OpenClaw supports one user or trust boundary per Gateway and does not claim hostile multi-tenant isolation inside one shared Gateway.
Prompt injection is not solved by system prompts alone; hard enforcement depends on tool policy, approvals, sandboxing, and channel allowlists.
Sandbox determines where tools run, tool policy determines which tools are available, and elevated is an exec-only path outside the sandbox that does not grant additional tools.
The Gateway owns the Cron scheduler, while heartbeat is intended for periodic context-aware checks and cron is intended for exact or isolated scheduled work.

Peter Steinberger stated in February 2026 that his next mission was to build an agent his mother could use, requiring broader safety work, and that OpenClaw would remain open and independent under a foundation.
